event: The car lets the three of them off in the dark, at the end of a lane too narrow for it.
They walk up through cedar and wet stone toward a single paper lantern over a door.
A woman lets them in, presses the key into Rumi's palm, bows and goes back down the lane.
No staff, no cameras, no fans at a barricade, no manager texting tomorrow's schedule.
Rumi stands holding the key, in a quiet so total it has texture.
For the first time in maybe three years, nobody in the world knows exactly where she is.
Mira toes off her shoes: this is either the most relaxing night of her life or a horror movie.
Zoey says it's the relaxing one; Mira says that's exactly what the first victim says.
Mira is smiling and has set her bag down to stay; Rumi's shoulders come loose a notch.
With these two alone, Rumi doesn't have to be the leader.
Rumi says, "Come on. The water's supposed to be the whole point."
The changing room is small, warm and lined in pale wood.
They have undressed before each other a thousand times, but always in a rush.
Now there is no countdown and no call time, only a quiet room and a long night.
Zoey goes first, unselfconscious, folding her clothes into a neat square on the bench.
Mira follows with an unfunny joke about communal nudity, to keep the air from getting heavy.
Rumi sees straight through Mira's joke, and loves her for it.
Rumi's hands stop at the hem of her shirt.
It isn't modesty but the marks up her forearms, across her back and down her ribs.
She has always kept them covered, sure they make her too much, even monstrous.
She takes the shirt off anyway, tired of being the only one in any room still hiding.
The marks catch the warm light, and she makes herself stand straight under it.
Nobody flinches; Mira looks openly, her face soft and a little stunned.
Zoey smiles: "I've never seen them in the light before."
Zoey says they're like the patterns on a moth's back, the kind you can't look away from.
Rumi nearly cries; she wraps a towel round herself and says, "Water."
She leads them out, all her covering left behind on the bench.
The bath is a long low room of dark stone, lit gold, with steam standing in the air.
The drifting steam turns the three of them from sharp to watercolor and back.
They go into the big sunken soaking pool, hissing at the heat, then surrendering to it.
The water takes the weight out of Rumi; her marks go under, and she no longer minds.
For a while nobody talks; water trickles over stone somewhere, and they breathe.
Mira tips her head back on the pool's lip, eyes closed, and Rumi catches herself looking.
Rumi makes herself stop, and doesn't entirely; she has been not-quite-stopping for years.
She remembers holding a look too long at Mira, laughing in a green room at two in the morning.
She remembers Zoey fixing her collar before a show, a hand at her pulse a second too long.
She decided it could never be anything: she leads, and wanting one would break the three.
Underneath, she was sure Mira and Zoey were the gravity, and she was the spare.
Across the pool, through the steam, Zoey is watching her.
Zoey caught her looking at Mira, and then Rumi caught Zoey catching her.
The steam thins at the wrong moment; there's nowhere to look that isn't one of the others.
Mira, eyes closed, says the energy just changed and she won't be the only one not informed.
At Rumi's suggestion they move to the wash stations: low stools, hand-showers, wooden buckets.
Zoey picks up the little bottle and says, "Rumi, turn around."
Zoey works soap into Rumi's hair, slow and thorough, and Rumi's eyes close.
Zoey's fingers trace one of the marks across Rumi's shoulder blade, following its shape.
Rumi asks, low, whether seeing them bothers her.
"No. I've wanted to look at them for years. You never let anyone close enough."
Mira, rough-voiced, asks to be next: she can't do the quiet thing, so somebody touch her.
Rumi rinses her hair, then kneels on the warm wet stone and washes Mira's back.
Mira goes genuinely quiet, the sharpness leaving her shoulders under Rumi's hands.
Zoey settles close, her knee against Rumi's, and says softly, "There she is."
"Shut up," Mira says, with no force; then, almost lost under the water: "Thank you."
Nobody is washing anyone now; they sit at the edge of the thing, waiting for one to say it.
Zoey says she'll say it, because the other two would circle it until the water goes cold.
Zoey says she is in love with both of them, the real kind, carried so long she stopped noticing.
She's sure she isn't the only one, and she's tired of all three pretending not to see.
The silence is the most frightening of Rumi's life, and then it opens instead of breaking.
Mira's voice cracks: she thought it was the two of them, and she was the one tagging along.
Rumi had the same story with a different cast: she thought it was Mira and Zoey.
She never wanted either out loud: she's the leader, she holds the shape, not one in the middle.
Zoey, crying and laughing: "You absolute idiots. All three of us thought we were the spare."
Rumi starts laughing too, helplessly, the relief coming out of her half a sob.
Mira: "It's not two and one. Any way you cut it." Rumi: "No. It's three."
Rumi reaches for both at once, Mira's hand in her right and Zoey's in her left, and pulls.
The three fold in together on the warm wet stone until there's no space left between them.
Zoey, the bravest, gives the first kiss to Rumi, tentative and then sure.
Mira goes still beside them; Rumi turns and kisses her too, at once, on purpose.
Then Zoey and Mira kiss, and a hand always reaches back so none of them is left watching.
They move near the pool, where the stone is heated underneath and the steam comes up thick.
It is clumsy in places, three not two; they laugh at stray elbows and whisper "here, like this."
They keep asking with looks and pauses, and waiting for yes, and nobody performs.
They go to Mira first, laying her back on the warm stone.
Rumi kisses down Mira's throat to her breast; Zoey licks her cunt, slow and patient.
Mira's hand flies into Zoey's hair, and she makes sounds without a single joke against them.
Mira comes, arching off the stone, a name in her gasp; Zoey murmurs, "We've got you."
Then Zoey: Mira holds her from behind, an arm across her collarbone, mouth at her neck.
Rumi kneels between Zoey's knees and fucks her with her fingers, then puts her mouth on her.
"Just feel it," Rumi tells her; Zoey, who always gives, lets herself be the one received.
Zoey comes with a sound that is almost a sob, shaking at being taken care of.
After, lips at her hip, Rumi tells her she doesn't always have to be the brave one.
Then Rumi, laid down between them, bare in good light, the marks and all of it.
Mira's fingertips follow the marks down her ribs as if they were the point, not the flaw.
Zoey kisses along a mark across Rumi's collarbone and down her center, as if reading it.
Zoey's fingers slide deep inside her while Mira's mouth closes warm over her breast.
Wholly seen and found wanted, Rumi comes saying both their names, and they say hers.
Done taking turns, they come back together, each with her hands on both the others.
It crests through all three at once, or near enough, and they hold each other up, laughing.
After, they lie tangled in the shallow end of the pool, the water up to their chests.
Rumi's head is on Mira's shoulder, Zoey tucked into both; Rumi loses track of where she ends.
The steam thins as the night goes on; a single high window shows a square of true night.
Nobody reaches for a joke, not even Mira; the quiet doesn't need filling anymore.
Mira keeps waiting to feel weird about this, and doesn't. "Me either," Zoey murmurs.
Rumi thinks she might not put the long sleeves and high collar back on tonight, maybe ever.
Into Mira's throat she says she didn't think she could be looked at, held still, in the light.
Zoey's arm tightens: "And?" Rumi: "And you didn't flinch."
"No," Zoey says simply. "Why would we."
When the water cools they get out and wrap each other in towels, with absurd care.
They pad back to the warm wooden room: not a leader and her two, just three.
